articles.title: Garrison welcomes new senior enlisted advisor
articles.summary: FORT HOOD, Texas — U.S. Army Garrison-Fort Hood held a change of responsibility Friday at III Armored Corps Headquarters, passing responsibility from Command Sgt. Maj. Loyd Rhoades to Command Sgt. Maj. Kristopher Tate.

articles.title: US Army seeks manufacturers for 155mm howitzer barrels amid boost in demand
articles.summary: The move comes amid Pentagon concerns that the U.S. government’s only plant for manufacturing howitzer barrels can’t keep up with the recent demand.

articles.title: Historic Accord: Naval Weapons Station Yorktown and Federally Recognized Native American Tribes Sign Landmark NAGPRA Agreement
articles.summary: WPNSTA Yorktown, located in the heart of Virginia's Historic Triangle, recently signed a binding NAGPRA agreement with federally recognized Native American Tribes. The agreement is the first of its kind within any U.S. Navy installation within the Commander, Navy Region Mid-Atlantic Area of Responsibility.

articles.title: ASC awards top ammo inspectors for munitions safety
articles.summary: Three employees from U.S. Army Sustainment Command have been recognized as Quality Assurance Specialist (Ammunition Surveillance) of the Year for their role in munitions safety and quality.

articles.title: U.S. Air Force Band kicks off Montana fall tour
articles.summary: The U.S. Air Force Concert Band and Singing Sergeants launched their autumn tour with a performance at the Alberta Bair Theater in Billings, Montana, Oct. 14.

articles.title: Cleveland Harbor Fall Dredging Starting; Supports Safe Great Lakes Navigation, Strengthens Local and National Economy
articles.summary: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Buffalo District, will begin fall dredging this week in Cleveland Harbor to maintain safe and navigable waterways for Great Lakes commercial vessels, recreational boaters and other harbor users on Lake Erie. The Buffalo District awarded an $11.7 million contract in April 2026 to New York-based DMYLES, Inc.

articles.title: ‘Ability to strike back’: Denmark commits to long-range missile orders
articles.summary: Copenhagen said it would purchase Joint Strike Missiles for its F-35s and a new ground-launched munition from an American firm.

articles.title: Trump, Putin negotiate release of US Air Force veteran from Russian prison
articles.summary: Stephen Hubbard, a retired teacher and U.S. Air Force veteran, was released from Russian custody on Wednesday after spending over four years in prison.

articles.title: Pentagon, Lockheed agree to 10-year deal for 850 F-35 jets
articles.summary: The decade-long framework guarantees at least 850 F-35 Lightning II fighters for the U.S. military, pending congressional approval and funding.

articles.title: Energy Action Month: Modern Technologies Strengthen Army Reserve Readiness and Energy Security
articles.summary: During Energy Action Month, the U.S. Army Reserve highlights significant advancements in energy efficiency, resilience, and cybersecurity that directly support this year’s theme: Secure Energy. Ready Forces. American Dominance.

articles.title: South Dakota Guard's 155th Engineer Company honored before southern border deployment
articles.summary: More than 120 Soldiers of the South Dakota Army National Guard's 155th Engineer Company were honored at an activation ceremony Oct. 22 at Wagner Community School. The Soldiers are deploying to the southern border in support of Operation Ardent Vanguard. The Wagner-based unit will deploy under the direction of U.S. Northern Command.

articles.title: The Pentagon has gone too far in using the Other Transaction Authority. Congress should act.
articles.summary: Created in 1958 for NASA, the obscure fiscal tool has since become the predominant approach to military contracting – at great risk to taxpayers, one researcher warns.

articles.title: Army Corps sorts things out and saves tax-payer money, Atomic Cleanup Program
articles.summary: Soon, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District will be cleaning up the Middlesex Municipal Landfill FUSRAP site in Middlesex, New Jersey and applying an innovative soil sorting system that will save tax-payer money, reduce air pollution, and most importantly return the land back to the community.

articles.title: Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group Sails in the Philippine Sea for Keen Sword Drills
articles.summary: The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group, as well as Japanese, Australian, Canadian and French warships, have gathered in the Philippine Sea to participate in exercise Keen Sword 27.

articles.title: US Army long-range fires make a splash on the frontline with China
articles.summary: The U.S. Army has been upgrading its missiles and rocket artillery, largely in response to China's missile arsenal.

articles.title: Multi-century U.S.-Dutch history focal point of latest CGSC International Hall of Fame induction
articles.summary: Dutch Lt. Gen. Jan-Willem Maas, commanding general of Joint Forces Command, Netherlands, was inducted into the U.S. Army Command and General Staff College International Hall of Fame during a ceremony Oct. 16, 2026, at the Lewis and Clark Center, Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.

articles.title: U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Mexican Navy Conclude 10th Annual Maritime Staff Talks
articles.summary: MEXICO CITY – Senior leaders from the U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, and the Mexican Navy (Marina) concluded the 10th Annual Maritime Staff Talks (MST) in Mexico City, Oct. 20-21, 2026, reinforcing a decade of sustained partnership and deepening security cooperation.

articles.title: The Pentagon wants ketamine wafers as a battlefield medicine option
articles.summary: The Pentagon awarded a multi-million-dollar contract to the Singapore-based iX Biopharma to develop a small, ketamine-packed wafer.

articles.title: Jackson, USACE breaks ground on new child center
articles.summary: Fort Jackson and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers broke ground Oct. 20 on a new child development center that is a sign of the commitment to its families and to Army readiness.

articles.title: Pentagon ignored cybersecurity flaws before data breach, Marines’ lawsuit says
articles.summary: A pair of Marines filed a class-action lawsuit Tuesday against the Pentagon over a data breach at the Defense Manpower Data Center.

articles.title: Pentagon, Lockheed agree to decade-long F-35 framework deal for hundreds of jets
articles.summary: The tentative agreement, which still needs lawmakers’ blessing, covers production and sustainment over the 10 years.

articles.title: 156th Wing optometrist bridges healthcare gaps, earns national award
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS, Nevada — U.S. Air Force Lt. Col. Alex Garcia, an optometrist assigned to the 156th Medical Group, Puerto Rico Air National Guard, was named the Reserve/Guard Optometrist of the Year by the Armed Forces Optometric Society during the 2026 AFOS Convention in Las Vegas, Nevada, Sept. 15–20, 2026.

articles.title: Right time, right place, right Airman
articles.summary: AVIANO AIR BASE, Italy— In a moment, an ordinary drive to work became an emergency. On the morning of August 26, 2026, U.S. Air Force Tech. Sgt. Danielle Smith, 31st Operational Medical Readiness Squadron medical technician, witnessed a vehicle accident in her Italian community. The car hit a utility pole and overturned.

articles.title: Ukraine to be able to buy military supplies via NATO agency: report
articles.summary: The deal comes amid worsening U.S.-Ukraine relations since U.S. President Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia this month to lower U.S. prices.

articles.title: USACE Far East District Hosts First Reverse Industry Day
articles.summary: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers – Far East District (USACE FED) Contracting Division hosted its first Reverse Industry Day (FEDRID), Oct. 6, 2025, in Suwon, South Korea. Over 250 attendees attended the event.

articles.title: 5th Air Naval Gunfire Liaison Company, Japan Ground Self-Defense Force strengthen partnership through joint fires training
articles.summary: U.S. Marines with 5th Air Naval Gunfire Liaison Company, III Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group, evaluated Japan Ground Self-Defense Force joint terminal attack controllers during training at Camp Hansen and the W-174 Joint Okinawa Training Range Complex, Okinawa, Japan, Sept. 14-17, 2026.
